draft.title: Physical development
card: Physical development is the change in the body and its systems over time, such as the bones, muscles, hormones and the organs that allow movement and reproduction.
It happens at every stage of the lifespan. Babies gain control of their muscles, and in old age muscle mass and bone strength tend to decline.
In youth, the body goes through a growth spurt, a fast increase in height and weight. Puberty is the time when the body becomes able to reproduce, driven by hormones.
Puberty brings changes such as a deeper voice, body hair and the start of periods. Young people begin puberty at different ages, and this is normal.
draft.remember: Physical development is change in the body and its systems, and youth brings a growth spurt and puberty.

a.q: Which of these is an example of physical development in youth?
opts: Hormones trigger puberty and a growth spurt begins
A teenager learns to manage anger in a calm way
A teenager makes a new group of friends at school
A teenager learns to solve harder maths problems
a.why: Hormone changes and a growth spurt are changes in the body, so they are physical development. Making friends is social development, and managing anger is emotional development. Solving harder problems is intellectual development.
a.clue: Look for the change that happens in the body.

b.q: Leila is 13 and has grown 8 cm in a year. Her friend Sam is 13 and has not started puberty yet. What is the best explanation?
opts: Young people start puberty at different ages
Sam has a problem with his physical development
Leila has gone through puberty too early
Sam will never go through a growth spurt
b.why: Young people begin puberty at different ages, so a difference between two 13-year-olds is normal. Calling it a problem is tempting, but the card says different starting ages are normal.
b.clue: Think about whether everyone starts puberty at the same age.

a.best: Hormones trigger puberty and a growth spurt begins

b.best: Young people start puberty at different ages

proposal.remember: Physical development is change in the body and its systems, and youth brings a growth spurt and puberty.

a.q: Which of these is an example of physical development in youth?
opts: A teenager's hormones trigger a fast gain in height
A teenager learns to manage anger in a calm way
A teenager makes a new group of friends at school
A teenager learns to solve harder maths problems
a.why: A hormone-driven gain in height is a change in the body, so it is physical development. Managing anger, making friends and solving harder problems are changes in feelings, relationships and thinking, not in the body.
a.clue: Look for the change that happens in the body.

b.q: Leila and Sam are both 13. Leila has grown 8 cm in a year, but Sam has not started puberty yet. What best explains the difference between them?
opts: Each body follows its own timing, which is normal
Sam's physical development is behind and needs treatment
Leila's growth spurt means she started puberty too early
Sam has missed his chance to have a growth spurt
b.why: Puberty and the growth spurt start at different ages for different young people, so a gap between two 13-year-olds is normal. Thinking Sam is behind and needs treatment is tempting, but a later start is not a sign of a problem.
b.clue: Think about what is typical, not what is identical.
